# zhetrd_he2hb

> Reduces a complex Hermitian matrix `A` to complex Hermitian band-diagonal form `AB` by a unitary similarity transformation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhetrdHe2hb from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhetrd_he2hb';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhetrd_he2hb( order, uplo, N, kd, A, LDA, AB, LDAB, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super-/sub-diagonals of the reduced band matrix<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **out** · Output band-diagonal matrix |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, kd + 1)`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - kd</sub> | **out** · Output reflector scalar factors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAU` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ LWMIN</sub> | **out** · Workspace of at least the reference's minimum (and optimum) `max(1, N*kd + N*max(kd,32) + 2*kd*kd)` complex elements; `null` allocates that size |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the reduced matrix if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$. The reduced matrix is stored in the array `AB`.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. On exit, if `UPLO = 'U'`, the diagonal and first superdiagonal of A are overwritten by the corresponding elements of the tridiagonal matrix T, and the elements above the first superdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors; if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of A are over- written by the corresponding elements of the tridiagonal matrix T, and the elements below the first subdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors. See Further Details.
- `AB`: On exit, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.
- `TAU`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors (see Further Details).
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, or if `LWORK=-1`, `WORK(1)` returns the size of `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, kd + 1 )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhetrd_he2hb.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N, kd,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super-/sub-diagonals of the reduced band matrix<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output Hermitian matrix (complex-element strides) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **out** · Output band-diagonal matrix |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` (in complex elements) |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - kd</sub> | **out** · Output array of reflector scalar factors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride for `TAU` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAU` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ LWMIN</sub> | **out** · Workspace; length from `offsetWork` at least the reference's minimum (and optimum) `max(1, N*kd + N*max(kd,32) + 2*kd*kd)` complex elements when `N > 0`, including when `N <= kd+1` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the reduced matrix if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$. The reduced matrix is stored in the array `AB`.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. On exit, if `UPLO = 'U'`, the diagonal and first superdiagonal of A are overwritten by the corresponding elements of the tridiagonal matrix T, and the elements above the first superdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors; if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of A are over- written by the corresponding elements of the tridiagonal matrix T, and the elements below the first subdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors. See Further Details.
- `AB`: On exit, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.
- `TAU`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors (see Further Details).
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, or if `LWORK=-1`, `WORK(1)` returns the size of `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK must be sufficiently large

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zhetrd_he2hb()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHETRD_HE2HB`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zhetrd_he2hb.f).
-   On entry, the relevant triangle of `A` (upper or lower) contains the Hermitian input. On exit, that triangle contains the band entries within `kd` of the diagonal, plus the reflectors representing `Q` for the entries further from the diagonal.
-   The Fortran reference uses an `ILAENV2STAGE` query to size the workspace. This implementation ignores the `WORK` argument and allocates scratch buffers internally (sized for the chosen block factor).
-   The "quick return" path triggers when `N <= kd+1`, in which case `AB` receives a direct copy of the relevant triangle of `A` and no reflectors are computed.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable camelcase, no-console */

import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zhetrd_he2hb from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhetrd_he2hb';

const N = 6;
const kd = 2;
const A = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const ar = reinterpret( A, 0 );
const AB = new Complex128Array( ( kd + 1 ) * N );
const TAU = new Complex128Array( N - kd );
let idx, i, j;

// Build a small column-major Hermitian matrix A (real diagonal, conjugate-symmetric off-diagonal):
for ( j = 0; j < N; j++ ) {
	for ( i = 0; i < N; i++ ) {
		idx = (j * N) + i;
		if ( i === j ) {
			ar[ 2*idx ] = 10 + i;
			ar[ (2*idx) + 1 ] = 0.0;
		} else if ( i < j ) {
			ar[ 2*idx ] = 1.0 / ( j - i + 1 );
			ar[ (2*idx) + 1 ] = 0.25 / ( j - i + 1 );
		} else {
			ar[ 2*idx ] = 1.0 / ( i - j + 1 );
			ar[ (2*idx) + 1 ] = -0.25 / ( i - j + 1 );
		}
	}
}

// Reduce A to lower Hermitian band form AB:
const info = zhetrd_he2hb( 'column-major', 'lower', N, kd, A, N, AB, kd+1, TAU, 1, null );

console.log( 'info = %d', info );
console.log( 'AB (interleaved re/im) =' );
console.log( reinterpret( AB, 0 ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHETRD_HE2HB`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHETRD\_HE2HB reduces a complex Hermitian matrix A to complex Hermitian band-diagonal form `AB` by a unitary similarity transformation: $Q^H \, A \, Q = \mathrm{AB}$.

### Further Details

Implemented by Azzam Haidar.

All details are available on technical report, SC11, SC13 papers.

Azzam Haidar, Hatem Ltaief, and Jack Dongarra. Parallel reduction to condensed forms for symmetric eigenvalue problems using aggregated fine-grained and memory-aware kernels. In Proceedings of 2011 International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis (SC '11), New York, NY, USA, Article 8 , 11 pages. http://doi.acm.org/10.1145/2063384.2063394

A. Haidar, J. Kurzak, P. Luszczek, 2013. An improved parallel singular value algorithm and its implementation for multicore hardware, In Proceedings of 2013 International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis (SC '13). Denver, Colorado, USA, 2013. Article 90, 12 pages. http://doi.acm.org/10.1145/2503210.2503292

A. Haidar, R. Solca, S. Tomov, T. Schulthess and J. Dongarra. A novel hybrid CPU-GPU generalized eigensolver for electronic structure calculations based on fine-grained memory aware tasks. International Journal of High Performance Computing Applications. Volume 28 Issue 2, Pages 196-209, May 2014. http://hpc.sagepub.com/content/28/2/196

</section>
